name: AI Observatory
blurb: Live telemetry on the health of the field: release cadence, repository activity, uptime, GPU availability, funding, patents, and regulatory movement.

built.name: Model Release Cadence
built.detail: How fast new models are shipping, and by whom.

built.name: Repository Activity
built.detail: This section tracks GitHub star counts and push activity across 55 widely used open-source AI repositories, spanning frameworks like TensorFlow and PyTorch, inference tools like Ollama and llama.cpp, and newer agent projects like AutoGPT and browser-use.

built.name: Hugging Face Trends
built.detail: This section tracks Hugging Face model activity: total download volume across roughly 16,363 tracked models, the most-downloaded individual models, and the license types those models are published under.

built.name: API Uptime
built.detail: This section tracks measured uptime for 12 AI API providers, including Anthropic, OpenAI, Cohere, Groq, Cerebras, Deepgram, ElevenLabs, AssemblyAI, Stability AI, Baseten, Fireworks AI, and Lambda.

built.name: Cloud GPU and Compute Telemetry
built.detail: What can be lawfully measured about AI compute: quarterly capital expenditure from the seven companies whose capex is the buildout, read from their own XBRL facts on SEC EDGAR, plus GPU cloud service health and verified benchmark registries.

built.name: Funding Activity
built.detail: This section is meant to track capital flowing into AI companies by funding stage and sector.

built.name: Patent Filings
built.detail: This section tracks cumulative AI-related patent counts for 108 companies, ranking them by total portfolio size and charting how the combined total moves over time.

built.name: Security Incidents
built.detail: This section tracks open incidents reported on the status pages of 12 AI infrastructure and model providers, including Anthropic, OpenAI, Cohere, Lambda, Fireworks AI, Baseten, Deepgram, and ElevenLabs.

title: AI Observatory
answer: Live telemetry on the health of the field: release cadence, repository activity, uptime, GPU availability, funding, patents, and regulatory movement.

reading.body:
The health of the AI field is measured across eight streams, and the only one tied to physical buildout covers seven companies' capital expenditure.

The telemetry splits into two kinds of signal. Model releases, Hugging Face downloads, repository activity, patents, and funding describe what the software layer is doing. API uptime and security incidents describe whether services stay reachable. Compute appears in exactly one place, quarterly capex from seven companies read from their own SEC EDGAR filings, alongside GPU cloud service health and benchmark registries. That is the narrowest coverage of the eight, and it is the only direct read on buildings and power.

The counts show where the field's weight sits. Roughly 16,363 Hugging Face models are tracked against 55 open-source repositories, 108 companies with patent portfolios, 12 API providers, and 12 providers whose status pages feed the incident count. Model activity is measured at a scale two orders of magnitude larger than the infrastructure it runs on. If compute is the constraint, the observability is inverted: the most instrumented layer is the one furthest from the binding limit.

What this does not tell you is direction or magnitude. No capex figures, no uptime percentages, no download numbers, no incident counts are given here, only the scope of what is tracked. Funding Activity is described as intended rather than built, so capital flows into AI companies are not yet measured at all. The data establishes what is watched, not what is happening.
